title: DMA async copy phasing and kernel synchronization - Apr 2027
content:
Summary:

This is a working investigation into intermittent low GPU utilization observed during production microbatch runs for the token-generation path. The root hypothesis: poor phasing between host->device async memcpy (DMA) and small, short-lived kernels causes idle gaps and underutilized SMs, amplified when CUDA Graphs are used incorrectly and when pinned host pages are not used.

Why this matters:
- We’re seeing sustained end-to-end throughput regressions (~18% P50 token/sec drop) in tails of some workloads despite similar kernel runtime medians.
- Nsight captures show frequent 1–4 ms gaps between kernel launches where the GPU is idle (~30–40% GPU utilization during these windows).
- Improving overlap of copies and compute yields measurable throughput and latency improvements.

Testbed and config:
- HW: 1x A100-40GB, PCIe Gen4, Linux 5.19, driver 525.xx, CUDA 12.2.
- Runtime: latest serving-runtime branch dma-async-experiment (GITHUB:repo/rl-inference#3421).
- Workload: generation microbatch size 2, sequence length 1024, kv-cache enabled.
- Capture tool: Nsight Systems CLI capture cap-20270412-001 (90s capture), timeline resolution 1us.
- Repro captures: 6 runs across two boxes (one with NVLink, one PCIe).

What we measured (representative numbers from capture):
- Average kernel compute time per token chunk: 4.8 ms (sigma ~1.1 ms).
- async memcpy H2D (small pages) observed: avg 0.85 ms, peaks 3.4 ms.
- inter-kernel idle gap (gap between memcpy end and next kernel launch): 1.2–3.8 ms in bad runs.
- SM occupancy (per-kernel): reported 36% median, theoretical achievable ~78% with current kernel config.
- Warp efficiency: 78% median.
- Overall GPU util (duty cycle during busy window): 42% for bad runs, 64% after fixes.
- CUDA graph capture overhead: first capture ~2.6 ms, replay overhead ~0.9 ms additional serialization when graphs were rebuilt on CPU per batch.

Key observations from Nsight timeline (cap-20270412-001):
1) Copy/compute phasing: Many H2D memcpyAsync events appear on stream 2, kernel launches on stream 1. Because we failed to pair events with cudaStreamWaitEvent properly, compute streams wait for implicit synchronization points. Timeline shows memcpy finishes but kernel launch is not scheduled for another 1–2 ms.
2) Pinned vs pageable memory: In the baseline test, host buffers were not pinned; Nsight shows longer memcpy durations and higher variance. Pinning host pages reduced avg memcpy by ~3x and lowered variance significantly.
3) Small kernels + dispatcher overhead: We have many small kernels (0.4–1.2 ms) with significant CPU-side dispatch jitter. Doing cudaGraph capture reduces CPU overhead but our capture code recreated graphs per batch (serialize on CPU), causing a 0.4–0.9 ms stall on the critical path.
4) CUDA graph replay serialization: When graphs are not reused across identical batch shapes, the runtime reconstructs parts of the graph and this causes kernel-launch serialization visible as a vertical stripe of idle time in the timeline.
5) Stream priorities: Using a single priority for both copies and compute creates contention; with explicit stream priorities we could prioritize compute and allow copies to flow opportunistically without introducing host-side blocking.
6) NVLink vs PCIe: NVLink host-to-device cases had much lower memcpy variance and better overlap, improving utilization by ~10–15% compared to PCIe machine.

Micro-experiments and results:
- Experiment A (pinned host pages): pinning reduces H2D memcpy avg 0.85 ms -> 0.28 ms; end-to-end throughput +9%.
- Experiment B (separate copy/compute streams + events): switched to dedicated streams, used cudaEventRecord/cudaStreamWaitEvent to force tight handoff; reduced inter-kernel gap from 1.8 ms median to 0.25 ms; throughput +15%.
- Experiment C (cudaGraph reuse): changed code to prebuild graphs for the few common batch/seq-length shapes and reuse per-inference; reduced CPU serialization stalls from 0.9 ms -> 0.05 ms; throughput +7% and tail latency improved.
- Experiment D (kernel fusion): fused two small kernels (token scoring + softmax) into single larger kernel; occupancy improved from 36% -> 58%; single kernel runtime increased slightly but overall throughput +12% because of reduced kernels and lower scheduling overhead.

Root causes (summary):
- Host memory not pinned in some code paths -> slow, variable memcpy.
- Incorrect stream/event choreography that leaves small gaps between copy completion and compute start.
- Naive cudaGraph usage where graphs were built per batch shape instead of reused -> CPU-side serialization.
- Many small kernels with low occupancy leading to low SM utilization and higher relative scheduling overhead.

Actionable remediation (short-term):
1) Ensure critical H2D buffers are allocated as pinned memory (cudaHostAlloc) in hot-path code paths. Owner: Jonah Reed. Target: 2027-04-19.
2) Introduce canonical copy/compute stream pair in serving-runtime and enforce explicit cudaEventRecord/cudaStreamWaitEvent handoffs to eliminate ambiguous ordering. Owner: Asha Mehta. Target: 2027-04-21.
3) Build and cache cudaGraphs for the top N common shapes (N=6 for now). Ensure graphs are reused and not rebuilt on the hot path. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Target: 2027-04-25.
4) Small-kernel roadmap: profile and attempt kernel fusion for top 3 smallest kernels; prioritize those that run back-to-back with memcpy. Owner: Maya Liu. Target: design by 2027-05-02.
5) Add explicit telemetry: per-kernel occupancy, inter-kernel gaps, memcpy variance metrics to the Console dashboards for per-route breakdown. Owner: Observability team. Target: 2027-05-09.

Longer-term ideas / experiments to try:
- Explore CUDA graphs with multiple streams (stream capturing) and session-based graph reuse across variable sequence-lengths.
- Investigate page-locked region pooling to avoid repeated pin/unpin penalties for ephemeral buffers.
- Re-evaluate prefetch to GPU unified virtual addressing vs explicit pinned copies for small page workloads.
- Consider batching policy changes to reduce number of distinct small kernels per request (merge compute phases where latency SLOs allow).

Open questions / risks:
- Pinning memory increases GPU memory pressure when using too many pinned pages; we need a pooling strategy to avoid OOM scenarios under heavy concurrency.
- Graph reuse requires deterministic stream ordering and identical memory pointers/sizes across captures; supporting shapes with small variance may require graph families.
- Changes to kernel fusion can affect numerical precision and correctness; need unit tests and small-scale A/B.

Useful commands / references used during profiling:
- Nsight CLI capture: nsys profile --output cap-20270412-001 --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt --duration=90s --capture-range=none --force-overwrite --cuda-memory-allocs=true --gpu-metrics-device=0 --cpuctxsw=false 
- Quick occupancy check (dev): nvcc -Xptxas -v kernel.cu  # for register usage; library-based kernels used register-limits via compile flags.
- CUDA Graph API notes: ensure cudaGraphInstantiate + cudaGraphLaunch reuse pattern; avoid repeated cudaGraphCreate->cudaGraphHostNodeAdd sequences on hot path.

Immediate next steps I will run this week:
- Patch 1: enable pinned allocation fallback when hot-path allocator returns pageable (PR created: GITHUB:repo/rl-inference#3421).
- Patch 2: canonical stream pair and event-based handoff; bench and capture follow-up.
- Capture follow-up: NVLINK vs PCIe side-by-side runs with pinned pages + graph reuse to measure delta.

Appendix: quick timeline excerpt description (textual) from Nsight capture cap-20270412-001:
- 00:00:00.000 — batch A start (CPU enqueue).
- 00:00:00.120 — host->device memcpyAsync(stream=2) for KV chunk 1 starts.
- 00:00:00.121 — kernel launch (stream=1) scheduled but visible on timeline only at 00:00:00.990 (gap ~0.87 ms).
- 00:00:00.995 — kernel runs 4.2 ms; on completion, next memcpy begins immediately when pinned memory used.
- Observed vertical stripe pattern when graphs rebuilt: CPU thread enters graph-build path for ~0.6–1.1 ms creating serialized idle across all streams.

If you want the raw Nsight capture slices, I uploaded cap-20270412-001 to the shared capture bucket and referenced it in linked_artifacts. Next meeting: sync Thurs 2027-04-14 10:30am PT to review the pinned alloc + stream handoff bench results.

Notes to self: avoid changing allocator globally until pooled pinned strategy is implemented. Also verify that changes do not regress Dedicated-reserved instances where we sometimes have different NUMA/PCI topology.

End of notes.
